Total paid media spend in 2024 was about $12,427,182.04. I summed the five ad-platform tables for the 53 weeks whose Monday falls in 2024 (2024-01-01 to 2024-12-30):

| Channel | 2024 spend (USD) |
|---|---|
| Google | 7,494,150.11 |
| Display | 1,525,654.76 |
| LinkedIn | 1,421,789.47 |
| Meta | 1,104,494.64 |
| CTV | 881,093.06 |
| **Total** | **12,427,182.04** |

- **Data checks:** I found no null, zero or negative costs and no duplicate rows. I converted Google's cost from micros to dollars.
- **Excluded spend:** I left out partner fees and webinar costs because I don't have a definition that counts them as paid media. Say so if you want them included.

I can't answer this from the data. "Brand-role channels" needs a channel-role classification, and nothing in the tables defines one. There's no role or category column, and no mapping table.

The data does allow at least two readings, and they give different answers:
- **Brand search only:** the Google campaign `FH_Search_Brand`.
- **Brand-building channels:** this could mean CTV, YouTube, display and similar. Which channels count is a judgment call I'd be making up.

Also, "paid media spend" has no stated scope. It's unclear whether it includes partner fees, webinar costs or email. Tell me which channels count as brand-role and what counts as paid media, and I'll calculate it.

Display retargeting cost about $91.07 per platform-reported conversion in 2024. That is $1,525,654.76 of media cost divided by 16,752 conversions.

- **Conversions:** I counted post-click (2,496) and post-view (14,256) conversions together as "platform-reported". If you only want post-click conversions, the figure would be about $611.
- **Retargeting:** The data has one display table (`ads_display_weekly`) with no campaign or tactic column. I treated all display spend as retargeting, so the figure is only right if display is entirely retargeting. The media plan notes do describe display as the retargeting lever.
- **Period:** I used the 53 weeks whose Monday falls in 2024, from 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-30.

- **Acquisition:** I counted each opportunity with stage "Closed Won" and a close date in 2023, which gives 10,964 deals.
- **Cost:** I summed all 2023 spend across every channel with a cost, which comes to $13,871,986:

Brand paid search cost per lead on a last-touch basis in 2025 was about $60.25.

- **Spend:** $2,494,644.40 on the `FH_Search_Brand` Google campaign, summing the weeks whose Monday falls in 2025.
- **Leads:** 41,408 CRM leads created in 2025 with last-touch UTM source `google`, medium `cpc` and campaign `search_brand`. I matched these case-insensitively because the source data mixes "Google" and "google".
- **Definition:** I counted every lead as a lead, not only MQLs or SQLs. The question didn't define "lead", so this is my assumption.

Non-brand paid search's last-touch cost per lead rose 23.76% from 2023 to 2025, from about $104.33 to about $129.13.

| Year | Spend (USD) | Leads | Cost per lead (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 3,650,138 | 34,985 | 104.33 |
| 2024 | 4,344,161 | 39,069 | 111.19 |
| 2025 | 5,402,499 | 41,839 | 129.13 |

- **Spend:** I used the `FH_Search_NonBrand` campaign in `ads_google_weekly`, assigning each week to the year of its Monday.
- **Leads:** I counted CRM leads whose last-touch source, medium and campaign are `google`, `cpc` and `search_nonbrand`. The source data spells these with mixed capitalization, so I matched them case-insensitively.
- **Year assignment:** Leads are assigned to a year by their created date rather than by week. That can differ slightly from the Monday rule for leads created in the first or last days of a year.

YouTube's last-touch CPA in 2024 was about **$719.44**. That is $682,749.76 of spend divided by 949 leads.

- **Spend:** This is the FH_YouTube_Prospecting campaign in `ads_google_weekly`, summed over weeks whose Monday falls in 2024.
- **Conversions:** I counted CRM leads created in 2024 whose last-touch `utm_source` is youtube. Source values `youtube` and `YouTube` were combined. I did not use the platform-reported conversions (18,658), because those are not last-touch.
- **Assumption:** I treated a "conversion" as a lead. Your data doesn't say what counts as an acquisition. If you mean closed-won customers, there were 51 for 2024, giving about $13,387. Those 51 are deals that closed in 2024, matched to YouTube-sourced leads.

Affiliate last-touch ROAS for 2025 was about 2.45.

- **Revenue:** $1,326,870. This is the Closed Won opportunity amount for leads whose last-touch UTM medium is `affiliate`. That covers the `partner_network`, `Partner_Network` and `reseller` sources. I counted deals by close date in 2025.
- **Spend:** $541,734.55. This is the sum of `partner_fees` in `partners_weekly` for weeks starting 2025-01-06 through 2025-12-22. I assumed those partner fees are the full affiliate cost.
- **ROAS:** 1,326,870 / 541,734.55 ≈ 2.45.

I treated the lead's UTM fields as the last touch. The data has no separate touch history to check that against.

Blended cost per lead in Q4 2025 was about $57.10. That is $2,994,779 of total marketing spend divided by 52,445 CRM leads.

- **Period:** I used the 12 weeks whose Monday falls in Q4, from 2025-10-06 to 2025-12-22. Leads are CRM leads created from 2025-10-06 to 2025-12-28.
- **Spend:** Google $1,849,007, Display $322,910, LinkedIn $245,763, Meta $228,051, CTV $130,212, Partner fees $112,750 and Webinars $106,087. I counted every channel with a cost, because "blended" wasn't defined for me.
- **Narrower definition:** Counting paid media only (Google, LinkedIn, Meta, Display and CTV) would give about $52.93.
- **CTV gaps:** The CTV table has no rows for two of the 12 weeks.

LinkedIn generated about $2.99 of pipeline per dollar of spend in 2023 on a last-touch basis.

- **Pipeline:** I took this to be the total amount of all opportunities created in 2023, whatever their stage. The data has no explicit definition of pipeline, so this is my assumption. It comes to $3,851,930.
- **Last-touch attribution:** I counted an opportunity as LinkedIn's if its lead's `utm_source` is LinkedIn. I matched case-insensitively so "linkedin" and "LinkedIn" both count.
- **Spend:** LinkedIn cost for weeks starting in 2023 was $1,286,948.92.

$3,851,930 ÷ $1,286,948.92 ≈ 2.99.

If you attribute by the lead's creation year instead of the opportunity's, pipeline is $3,838,190. The ratio is still about 2.98.

Partners (the affiliate channel) had the lowest last-touch CPA in 2025, at about $1,318.

- **Partners:** $541,735 in partner fees against 411 closed-won deals, giving about $1,318. That count includes both partner_network (332) and reseller (79) as affiliate sources. Counting only partner_network gives about $1,632, which is still the lowest.
- **Google search:** about $2,179 ($7.90M over 3,624 deals).
- **Meta:** about $3,095 (Facebook plus Instagram, $1.07M over 346 deals).
- **LinkedIn:** about $3,631 ($1.14M over 313 deals).
- **Display:** about $5,800 ($1.68M over 289 deals).
- **YouTube:** about $16,649 ($566K over 34 deals).

I took last-touch to mean the lead's UTM source, and I counted deals by close date in 2025. I treated the video campaigns in the Google ads table as YouTube spend and the search campaigns as Google search. CTV is excluded because it has spend but no UTM source on leads, so it has no last-touch deals.

ive you a true incremental CPA for Connected TV in 2025 from these tools. Doing so would mean estimating it, and the data has no definition or experiment to anchor an estimate.

- **No lift test exists.** Nothing in the data holds out CTV for a randomized or matched control group. `ctv_weekly` has spend, impressions, completed views and `attributed_leads`, which are the platform's own attribution counts and don't show what CTV caused. Dividing 2025 CTV spend by those leads would give an attributed CPA, not an incremental one.
- **The CTV flights can't be read as an experiment.** In 2025, CTV ran in eight regions (CMH, CVG, DSM, MKE, MLI, MSN, MSP, TOL), each for only a handful of weeks. Those on-weeks are not randomly chosen. Regions averaged more CRM leads in their CTV weeks than in their non-CTV weeks, but I can't tell how much of that is CTV and how much is the timing of the flights. `media_plan_changes` shows budget moves that overlap with other channels, and `fleet_activity_index_weekly` shows demand shifts.
- **The conversion isn't defined.** I don't have a definition of what counts as an incremental conversion (a lead, an MQL, an SQL or closed-won revenue). I also don't have a rule for the control group or for the demand adjustment. Any number would depend on those choices.

I can report the attributed CTV CPA for 2025 instead, or build a flight-vs-non-flight comparison if you give me the conversion definition and the method you want.

I can't calculate 2025 gross margin from the data I have. Gross margin needs revenue and cost of goods sold (hosting, support, delivery and similar). None of the tables has COGS or any other cost-of-delivery field.

The tables hold marketing data:
- Ad spend, by channel.
- Partner fees.
- Webinar costs.
- CRM leads and opportunity amounts.

Opportunity amounts could stand in for revenue, and the spend columns cover marketing costs. Marketing spend isn't COGS, though, so using it would give a number that isn't gross margin. I also don't have your definition of which costs count toward it.

If you can send a COGS table or tell me which costs to include, I can rerun this.

I can't give you a customer lifetime value for paid search deals, because the data doesn't have what a lifetime value calculation needs.

- **What the data has:** `crm_opportunities` holds one amount per deal, with a stage of Closed Won or Closed Lost. Paid search deals (utm_medium cpc, source google) average about $2,830 per Closed Won deal.
- **What's missing:** There is no data on renewals, recurring revenue, churn or retention, customer tenure, or gross margin. I also don't have your definition of lifetime value, such as the time horizon, whether it's revenue or margin, or whether it's discounted.

The $2,830 is only a first-deal amount. Calling it lifetime value would be a guess. If you can give me retention or churn data and a definition, I can work it out.
